name: Worn by feet
describes: Floor stone where people walk, most at thresholds and on stair treads: grit under shoes scratches the polish off first, then wears the stone into a shallow dish, and edges round.

mechanism.text: Shoes carry mineral grit onto the floor. Quartz (Mohs 7) is far harder than calcite (Mohs 3), so each step drags harder grains across the stone and ploughs fine scratches.
mechanism.source: Anthony J.W., Bideaux R.A., Bladh K.W., Nichols M.C. (eds.) Handbook of Mineralogy, Mineralogical Society of America, 'Quartz' (Mineral Data Publishing, version 1.2, 2001), http://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/quartz.pdf ; Anthony J.W., Bideaux R.A., Bladh K.W., Nichols M.C. (eds.) Handbook of Mineralogy, Mineralogical Society of America, 'Calcite' (Mineral Data Publishing, version 1, 2001-2005), http://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/calcite.pdf

mechanism.text: Worn volume grows with load times sliding distance, divided by the hardness of the worn surface and multiplied by a wear coefficient: V = K W s / H.
mechanism.source: Archard J.F. (1953) 'Contact and rubbing of flat surfaces', Journal of Applied Physics 24:981-988, https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1721448

glossLoss.text: Gloss rises steeply as roughness falls in polishing, so the first scratches take a polish down steeply; the relation is weaker in travertine.
glossLoss.source: Yavuz H., Ozkahraman T., Demirdag S. (2011) 'Polishing experiments on surface quality of building stone tiles', Construction and Building Materials 25:1707-1711, abstract as indexed (full text not read), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2010.10.016

voidsOpen.text: In cross-cut (fleuri) travertine, thin-walled cavities at or near the face may break open under heavy foot traffic after installation; filling them is accepted practice.

photograph: The polish goes first: dull lanes along the walking lines and a dull fan at each doorway, with the gloss surviving beside walls and in corners.
Treads and sills round at their arrises and dish in the middle, where feet land most.
In cross-cut travertine, voids open through the face along the busiest routes and are later filled.

searched: the sets listed in Substances/travertine.json and Substances/cream-marble.json, evidenceSearch
evidenceSearch.found: No photograph on this PC shows real worn, soiled or weathered travertine or cream marble.
evidenceSearch.tier: A tier (c) set of museum photographs at known exposure (worn thresholds, soiled open pores, weathered exterior travertine) would close the gap.

unverified.reason: No measured Archard wear coefficient for grit under shoes on travertine or Crema Marfil was found.
No measured wear depth per footfall (or per million footfalls) on a travertine or marble floor or threshold was read at its source.
No measured loss of gloss of a polished calcite floor against traffic was read.
